nodes.description: A heterozygous germline CASQ1 variant alters calsequestrin-1. Reported alleles are almost all missense, at conserved residues; p.Asp244Gly sits in a high-affinity calcium-binding site. A C-terminal frameshift that extends the protein has also been reported. The disease alleles reduce the calcium binding and storage of calsequestrin-1, its molecular function.

nodes.description: Calsequestrin-1 normally binds calcium and assembles into polymers that buffer calcium in the terminal cisternae next to RyR1. Disease alleles change this behaviour in two directions. p.Asp244Gly partially loses calcium binding at high calcium concentrations and aggregates abruptly instead of forming ordered polymers, while p.Asp44Asn and p.Gly103Asp show reduced calcium-dependent aggregation.

nodes.description: In older knock-in mice, mTORC1 signalling increases, autophagic flux falls and proteasomal clearance of aggregated proteins is inadequate, so insoluble ubiquitinated proteins and lysosomes accumulate. Younger mice clear the misfolded protein, and the authors attribute the late onset to this age-dependent decline in proteolytic capacity, which in turn sustains ER stress.

nodes.description: Calsequestrin-1 binds STIM1 and STIM2 and restrains store-operated calcium entry. Tubular aggregate alleles lose this restraint. The vacuolar p.Asp244Gly allele does not: knock-in mice carrying it show no increase in store-operated calcium entry, which is one reason the two presentations are modelled as separate branches.
